quality_guards: Wood-dust risk varies with wood type, process, dust concentration, duration, ventilation, cleaning method, RPE fit and worker susceptibility.
HSE wood-dust guidance is task-, material-, workplace-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level disease probability.
Chemical risk varies with formulation, concentration, application method, ventilation, exposure route, duration, PPE and individual susceptibility.
HSE woodworking-chemical guidance is substance-, process-, worker-, control-, premises- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level toxicity probability.
Dust-explosion risk depends on particle size, concentration, confinement, oxygen, ignition energy, ventilation, housekeeping and equipment condition.
HSE combustible-dust evidence is material-, process-, enclosure-, ignition-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level explosion probability.
Work-related stress varies with job design, workload, autonomy, support, relationships, role clarity, organisational change and individual circumstances.
HSE stress guidance is organisation-, team-, role-, worker-, intervention- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level mental-health probability.
Stress-control effectiveness depends on workload, staffing, management practice, worker participation, resources, job design and implementation quality.
The Management Standards describe organisational controls and do not provide a parcel-level estimate of stress, absence or injury.
Risk assessment outcomes depend on the actual hazard, people exposed, likelihood, severity, controls, maintenance and changing conditions.
HSE risk-assessment guidance is workplace-, task-, substance-, worker-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level risk score.
PPE performance depends on correct selection, compatibility, fit, condition, maintenance, training, supervision and consistent use.
HSE PPE guidance is hazard-, equipment-, wearer-, task-, maintenance- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level protection probability.
Measles transmission risk depends on infectious period, proximity, duration, ventilation, immunity, vaccination, age and response timing.
UKHSA case-management guidance is case-, contact-, setting-, immunity-, intervention- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Surveillance counts are affected by case definitions, testing, reporting delays, geography, age structure, immunity and publication date.
UKHSA dashboard data are population surveillance snapshots and must not be treated as exact parcel-level infection probability.
Food-recall risk depends on product, batch, hazard, distribution, consumption, allergen sensitivity, recall reach and response timing.
FSA recall guidance is product-, batch-, business-, consumer-, communication- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level illness probability.
Cosmetic risk depends on formulation, concentration, contamination, labelling, user sensitivity, use pattern, storage and product authenticity.
OPSS consumer guidance is product-, ingredient-, user-, supply-chain-, compliance- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level harm probability.
A reported undesirable effect can reflect individual allergy or sensitivity and does not automatically establish product noncompliance.
OPSS notification evidence is product-, event-, user-, clinical-, regulatory-, corrective-action- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level harm probability.
Product-alert relevance depends on exact model, batch, defect, jurisdiction, user, use conditions, corrective action and publication status.
OPSS alerts are product- and incident-specific and must not be converted directly into parcel-level harm probability.
Medicine or device risk depends on product, batch, indication, dose, patient, user, defect, corrective action and clinical context.
MHRA communications are product-, batch-, patient-, user-, action- and time-specific and are not an exact parcel-level harm probability.
Lithium-battery aviation risk depends on chemistry, rating, manufacture, damage, packing, baggage location, cargo handling, operator controls and flight context.
CAA dangerous-goods evidence is battery-, shipment-, passenger-, operator-, aircraft-, control- and time-specific and is not a parcel-level fire probability.
Rail risk depends on infrastructure, rolling stock, signalling, traffic, maintenance, competence, public behaviour, reporting and operational context.
ORR railway evidence is operator-, route-, asset-, worker-, passenger-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level incident probability.
